title: Count Substrings That Differ by One Character
summary: Given two strings s and t, determine the count of non-empty substrings in s that can be altered by changing a single character to match some substring in t exactly.
statement: Given two strings s and t, determine the count of non-empty substrings in s that can be altered by changing a single character to match some substring in t exactly. This means finding substrings in s that differ from any substring in t by only one character. For instance, 'computer' and 'computation' differ by one character ('e' and 'a'). The task is to count all such matching substrings.
constraints: s and t contain 1 through 100 lowercase letters.
Count pairs of equal-length nonempty substrings that differ at exactly one aligned position.
Occurrences at different starting positions count separately.
hints: Each pair of substring starts lies on one alignment diagonal.
On a diagonal, remember the latest and second-latest mismatch positions.
Every ending position has latest-second_latest starts that include exactly the latest mismatch.
Starts after the second-latest mismatch exclude all earlier differences, while starts at or before the latest mismatch include the required one.
editorial: Starts after the second-latest mismatch exclude all earlier differences, while starts at or before the latest mismatch include the required one.

tests.explanation: Across all aligned diagonals, six substring pairs have exactly one mismatched character.
The pairs a/b, ab/bb, and a/b from the second position give three valid occurrences.
